title: Job Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 31.

questions.question: In Job 31, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I made a covenant with mine eyes
Let me be weighed in an even balance
If my step hath turned out of the way
If I did despise the cause of my manservant
questions.correctAnswer: I made a covenant with mine eyes
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in the chapter, found in Job 31:1.

questions.question: What did Job say he made with his eyes?
questions.explanation: Job specifically states in Job 31:1 that he made a covenant with his eyes.

questions.question: According to Job, what is the portion of God from above?
questions.explanation: Job asks about the inheritance of the Almighty from on high in Job 31:2.

questions.question: What does Job suggest is destruction for the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job questions if destruction is not a punishment for the wicked in Job 31:3.

questions.question: What does Job believe God does regarding his ways?
questions.explanation: Job asserts that God sees his ways and counts all his steps in Job 31:4.

questions.question: What does Job ask to be weighed in?
questions.explanation: Job requests to be weighed in an even balance for God to know his integrity in Job 31:6.

questions.question: What does Job say will happen if his heart has been deceived by a woman?
options: His wife will grind for another
questions.correctAnswer: His wife will grind for another
questions.explanation: Job states that if his heart has been deceived, then let his wife grind unto another in Job 31:10.

questions.question: What does Job call it if he despises the cause of his servants?
questions.explanation: Job declares it a heinous crime and an iniquity to be punished by judges in Job 31:11.

questions.question: What does Job say would root out all his increase?
questions.explanation: Job states that it is a fire that consumeth to destruction and would root out all his increase in Job 31:12.

questions.question: What does Job ask he will answer when God rises up?
questions.explanation: Job questions what he shall answer when God visits him in Job 31:14.

questions.question: Job made a covenant with his eyes to avoid thinking upon whom?
questions.explanation: Job explicitly states in Job 31:1 that he made a covenant with his eyes to not think upon a maid.

questions.question: True or False: Job believes that God counts all his steps.
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 31:4 that God counts all his steps.

questions.question: True or False: Job claims he has walked with vanity.
questions.explanation: Job mentions in Job 31:5 about walking with vanity.

questions.question: True or False: Job believes that only the righteous are punished.
questions.explanation: Job questions if destruction is not for the wicked in Job 31:3, implying that the wicked are punished.

questions.question: True or False: Job states that he has never wronged his servants.
questions.explanation: Job questions what he will do if he has despised the cause of his servants in Job 31:13, implying he might have wronged them.

medium.title: Job Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Job 31:15, who is the maker of both Job and others in the womb?
options: He that made me in the womb
questions.correctAnswer: He that made me in the womb
questions.explanation: Job 31:15 specifically states 'Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?' referring to the maker of both Job and others.

questions.question: What does Job 31:22 promise will happen if Job has lifted his hand against the fatherless as mentioned in Job 31:21?
options: Let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone
questions.correctAnswer: Let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone
questions.explanation: Job 31:22 follows Job 31:21 and states the consequence if he lifted his hand against the fatherless: 'Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.'

questions.question: What does Job 31:23 say was a terror to Job, causing him to be unable to endure it?
questions.explanation: Job 31:23 declares 'For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.'

questions.question: How do Job 31:16 and Job 31:17 relate to Job's care for the poor and fatherless?
options: Withholding from the poor or eating alone without sharing is condemned
Avoiding interaction with widows is advised
questions.correctAnswer: Withholding from the poor or eating alone without sharing is condemned
questions.explanation: Job 31:16-17 condemn withholding from the poor or eating alone without sharing with the fatherless, emphasizing care and provision for them.

questions.question: According to Job 31:19-20, what did Job provide to those who lacked clothing and warmth?
options: Clothing and fleece of his sheep for warmth
questions.correctAnswer: Clothing and fleece of his sheep for warmth
questions.explanation: Job 31:19-20 states that Job ensured the poor were clothed and warmed with the fleece of his sheep.

questions.question: What does Job 31:24 warn against making one's hope and confidence?
questions.explanation: Job 31:24 warns against making gold and fine gold one's hope and confidence.

questions.question: In Job 31:14, what question does Job ask concerning his treatment of servants when they contended with him?
options: Did I give them extra wages?
questions.explanation: Job 31:13-14 addresses whether Job despised the cause of his servants when they contended with him.

questions.question: How does Job 31:25 describe his reaction to wealth and gain?
options: Rejoicing because his wealth was great
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoicing because his wealth was great
questions.explanation: Job 31:25 states 'If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;' indicating that rejoicing over wealth is considered in this context.

questions.question: What does Job 31:26-28 caution against in relation to the sun, moon, and secret desires of the heart?
options: Being secretly enticed or denying God above
Praising the sun and moon openly
questions.correctAnswer: Being secretly enticed or denying God above
questions.explanation: Job 31:26-28 warns that secret enticement of the heart or denying God above is an iniquity to be punished.

questions.question: What does Job commit to doing if he has walked in vanity or hastened to deceit according to Job 31:5-6?
options: Let me be weighed in an even balance so God may know my integrity
questions.correctAnswer: Let me be weighed in an even balance so God may know my integrity
questions.explanation: Job 31:5-6 says if he has walked with vanity or hastened to deceit, let him be weighed in an even balance that God may know his integrity.

questions.question: How does Job describe his relationship with the widow he guided from youth in Job 31:18?
options: As one who has guided her from his mother's womb, like a father
As a stranger who ignored her
As a servant who was commanded
As a competitor for her wealth
questions.correctAnswer: As one who has guided her from his mother's womb, like a father
questions.explanation: Job 31:18 describes that from his youth he brought up the widow as with a father and guided her from his mother's womb.

questions.question: According to Job 31:4, who sees and counts all of Job's ways and steps?
questions.explanation: Job 31:4 says 'Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?' referring to God.

questions.question: True or False: Job 31:14 questions what he should answer when God visits and rises up.
questions.explanation: Job 31:14 asks 'What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?' confirming the correct answer is True.

questions.question: True or False: Job 31:27 states that secretly enticed hearts and kisses to the hand are acceptable actions.
questions.explanation: Job 31:27 indicates that secret enticement and kissing the hand are considered sins to be punished, so the answer is False.

questions.question: True or False: Job 31:21 states that lifting the hand against the fatherless is acceptable if one sees their help in the gate.
questions.explanation: Job 31:21 condemns lifting the hand against the fatherless, even when one sees his own help in the gate, so the statement is False.

hard.title: Job Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 31.

questions.question: What did Job say about rejoicing at the destruction of those who hate him?
questions.explanation: Job 31:29 states that he did not rejoice at the destruction of him that hated him, showing his integrity.

questions.question: What did Job claim he never wished for with his mouth?
questions.explanation: In Job 31:30, Job asserts that he never suffered his mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.

questions.question: What did Job say about the men of his tabernacle concerning the flesh of his enemy?
questions.explanation: Job 31:31 indicates that the men of his tabernacle did not say, 'Oh that we had of his flesh!' showing his integrity and lack of malice.

questions.question: How did Job respond to strangers and travelers?
questions.explanation: Job 31:32 explains that Job opened his doors to the traveler, demonstrating his hospitality and kindness.

questions.question: What does Job imply about hiding transgressions in Job 31:33?
questions.explanation: Job 31:33 mentions that if he covered his transgressions as Adam did, he would be hiding his iniquity in his bosom, which implies wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does Job desire in Job 31:35?
questions.explanation: In Job 31:35, Job expresses his desire that someone would hear him and that the Almighty would answer him.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'covenant' in Job 31:1 mean?
questions.explanation: In Job 31:1, the term refers to a formal agreement or pact, particularly emphasizing the commitment Job made regarding his eyes.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Job 31:30 when Job discusses his mouth?
questions.explanation: Job 31:30 employs parallelism, contrasting the idea of wishing a curse with the integrity of his speech.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Job's integrity in Job 31:6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 11:1 echoes the theme of integrity and fairness, stating that a false balance is an abomination to the Lord, similar to Job's desire for God to weigh him in an even balance.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage reflects the theme of hospitality found in Job 31:32?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:2 encourages showing hospitality to strangers, resonating with Job's practice of opening his doors to travelers in Job 31:32.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Job 31:34?
questions.explanation: Job 31:34 follows Job's questioning of whether he feared a great multitude or the contempt of families, indicating his courage.

questions.question: In Job 31:9, what does Job mention regarding his heart?
questions.explanation: Job 31:9 refers to the possibility of his heart being deceived by a woman, highlighting his concern for moral integrity.

questions.question: Job states in Job 31:15 that both he and his servant were made by God. What does this imply about their value?
questions.explanation: Job 31:15 emphasizes that both Job and his servants were created by God, implying equality in their inherent value.

questions.question: Is it true that Job expressed a desire for God to answer him?
questions.explanation: Job's desire for an answer from God is clearly expressed in Job 31:35, verifying the statement.

questions.question: Is it false that Job rejoiced at the destruction of his enemies according to Job 31:29?
questions.explanation: Job 31:29 shows that he did not rejoice at the destruction of his enemies, making the statement false.

theological.title: Job Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 31:6 teach about human sanctification?
options: God examines human integrity with perfect justice
Sanctification is based on human works alone
Humans cannot be weighed by divine standards
questions.correctAnswer: God examines human integrity with perfect justice
questions.explanation: Job 31:6 states 'Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity,' emphasizing that God judges human integrity with perfect justice.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 31:15 teach regarding the imago Dei and human dignity?
options: All humans share a common divine origin and dignity
Only the righteous are created in God's image
Human dignity is based on social status
God fashions only the elect in the womb
questions.correctAnswer: All humans share a common divine origin and dignity
questions.explanation: Job 31:15 says 'Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?' teaching that all humans share a divine origin and inherent dignity.

questions.question: What doctrine about the fear of God is expressed in Job 31:23?
options: The terror of God's destruction instills reverent fear
Fear of God is unnecessary for the righteous
God's majesty does not affect human conscience
Fear of God leads to despair, not holiness
questions.correctAnswer: The terror of God's destruction instills reverent fear
questions.explanation: Job 31:23 states 'For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure,' indicating that reverent fear of God's majesty restrains sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 31:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 31:4 says 'Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?' demonstrating God's omniscience, His all-knowing nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Job 31:12?
questions.explanation: Job 31:12 compares sin to a consuming fire that 'would root out all mine increase,' reflecting God's holiness and intolerance of sin.

questions.question: How does Job 31 contribute to the biblical narrative arc regarding human righteousness and divine justice?
options: It exemplifies the plea for vindication based on personal righteousness before God
It teaches that human righteousness is irrelevant to divine justice
It rejects the possibility of human integrity in a fallen world
It advances the doctrine of salvation without works
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the plea for vindication based on personal righteousness before God
questions.explanation: Job 31 concludes with Job's detailed assertion of his righteousness and his desire for God’s vindication, fitting the biblical theme of human integrity before divine justice.

questions.question: In what way does Job 31:32 connect to the theme of hospitality in the redemptive history of Scripture?
options: It reflects the biblical mandate to welcome strangers as an act of righteousness
It condemns hospitality as a worldly distraction
It prioritizes family over strangers exclusively
It limits hospitality to covenant members only
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the biblical mandate to welcome strangers as an act of righteousness
questions.explanation: Job 31:32 states 'The stranger did not lodge in the street: but I opened my doors to the traveller,' echoing biblical hospitality themes seen in Abraham's story and the Law.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Job 31:16 and Job 31:20 teach about social justice?
options: The responsibility to provide for the poor and vulnerable is a divine mandate
Social justice is optional in the life of faith
Only the wealthy are accountable for justice
Justice pertains solely to religious rituals
questions.correctAnswer: The responsibility to provide for the poor and vulnerable is a divine mandate
questions.explanation: Job 31:16-20 emphasize caring for the poor, widow, and fatherless, underscoring divine expectation for social justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 31:9 and Job 31:10 teach about sexual ethics and covenant fidelity?
options: Adultery is a heinous sin punishable by human and divine judgment
Sexual sin is private and without social consequence
Covenant fidelity is unrelated to moral law
questions.correctAnswer: Adultery is a heinous sin punishable by human and divine judgment
questions.explanation: Job 31:9-11 state adultery is 'an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges,' demonstrating its serious covenantal breach.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine judgment and human accountability is taught in Job 31:38 and Job 31:40?
options: Sin brings tangible consequences and divine judgment upon the land and people
Divine judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions
Human actions do not affect the environment
Judgment only comes at the final eschaton
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brings tangible consequences and divine judgment upon the land and people
questions.explanation: Verses 31:38-40 warn that if Job exploited the land, it should produce thistles instead of wheat, symbolizing the real consequences of sin.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Job 31:13-15 ignores social equality by distinguishing masters from servants. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It upholds the equal creation and dignity of all humans, including servants
It teaches that servants have no claim to justice
It endorses social hierarchy without moral responsibility
It limits moral concern to one's own social class
questions.correctAnswer: It upholds the equal creation and dignity of all humans, including servants
questions.explanation: Job 31:13-15 demands justice for servants, reminding that God made both master and servant, affirming equal dignity under God.

questions.question: What doctrine about the dangers of idolatry is taught in Job 31:24?
options: Making wealth an object of trust is idolatry contrary to faith in God
Material wealth is the ultimate sign of God's favor
Idolatry includes only worship of physical statues
Gold is a neutral resource with no spiritual implications
questions.correctAnswer: Making wealth an object of trust is idolatry contrary to faith in God
questions.explanation: Job 31:24 warns against making 'gold my hope,' showing that placing confidence in wealth is idolatrous.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated in Job 31:14?
questions.explanation: Job 31:14 asks what Job will do when God rises up to judge, underscoring God's attribute of justice in holding humans accountable.

questions.question: What doctrine about the human conscience and divine law is expressed in Job 31:28?
options: Secret delight in sin equates to denial of God’s sovereignty
Sin can be hidden without consequence
Denial of God is unrelated to moral behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Secret delight in sin equates to denial of God’s sovereignty
questions.explanation: Job 31:28 condemns secret enticement and self-kissing of the hand as iniquity punishable by the judge, equating it with denying God above.

questions.question: How does Job 31:1 reflect on the doctrine of covenant faithfulness in sanctification?
options: Making a covenant with one's eyes shows intentional guarding against sin
Covenants are irrelevant to personal holiness
Sanctification is automatic without personal effort
Guarding the eyes is legalism, not true faith
questions.correctAnswer: Making a covenant with one's eyes shows intentional guarding against sin
questions.explanation: Job 31:1 mentions a covenant with the eyes to avoid lust, showing the role of intentional commitment in sanctification.
